correctness.rationale: Exact ordered-vertex links are K_{a,b} minus a common-neighbor matching. A leaf or degree at least five obstructs manifold links; a degree-four vertex must be universal and hence implies order five. For n>=7, any degree-three vertex forces a bipartite three-versus-four neighborhood contradiction. All n>=7 graphs must be cycles, whose complexes are annuli. All 33,864 labeled graphs for orders 3 through 6 are fully enumerated by a dependency-free checker, compared against full isomorphism orbits, and every valid cubical complex has exact component, orientation, boundary and Euler invariants calculated. All output matched. Infinite case relies on symbolic proof, not finite sampling.

value.rationale: The problem asks for a natural complete recognition and topological classification of ordered collision-free two-agent graph configurations as surfaces, extending a recent closed-only research direction. The result exhibits every possible boundary configuration up to graph isomorphism and computes exact genus and boundary circles. Strong exclusion of all other graph orders and several nontrivial positive boundary cases go beyond generic surface criteria or routine one-parameter substitution.
